text:
Priya S.: @Jamal customer 8421 says ~40% of `credential.create` events are missing from their SIEM for 2026-02-12 09:12–09:25 UTC. They attached the exported index and spot-checked counts.
Jamal R.: Can you paste the manifest names + tenant id and a quick repro? which export pipeline (s3->splunk vs. syslog) are they using?
Priya S.: tenant=8421, pipeline=s3->splunk (forwarder v2.4.1). Manifest they shared:
```
s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/tenant=8421/date=2026-02-12/shard=003/manifest-00023.json
s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/tenant=8421/date=2026-02-12/shard=004/manifest-00024.json
```
The manifest objects for shard 003 show zero-byte batch files in the listing, and splunk counts show gaps.
Support Oncall: quick triage - I pulled forwarder logs around that window. Snippet: 
```
2026-02-12T09:15:12Z forwarder[pid=72]: ERROR decrypt batch s3://.../batch-000234.gz: KMSDecryptFailed: InvalidCiphertextException
2026-02-12T09:15:12Z forwarder[pid=72]: WARN skipping batch batch-000234 (decrypt error)
```
This repeats a few times then the forwarder moves on. :frowning: 
Eng-Infra-Bot: kms-rotation-service: alias `alias/redwood-audit` rotated at 2026-02-12T09:14:58Z (rotation-id: rot-2026-02-12-091458).
Lucia M.: if the rotation happened at 09:14:58, that lines up. If the forwarder still has the old DEK cached, it can fail to decrypt recently rotated objects. Also check if there's a race where new objects are written with the new key while some writers still used old envelope.
Jamal R.: ok — two parallel asks: (1) confirm forwarder KMS client saw the new alias and reloaded keys; (2) check S3 put-time vs manifest generation. Can you run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit-exports --key <key>` for one of the batch files and paste x-amz-meta-kms-key and LastModified?
Priya S.: did that, example: 
```
Key: prod/tenant=8421/date=2026-02-12/shard=003/batch-000234.gz
LastModified: 2026-02-12T09:15:05Z
x-amz-meta-kms-key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222:kms/key/old-dek
x-amz-meta-envelope: enc-v2
ContentLength: 0
```
So that batch is zero bytes and metadata references the old key. The manifest still referenced it which is why splunk skipped it. Not sure why ContentLength==0 though — uploader should never write zero-byte batches.
Lucia M.: zero-byte sometimes indicates an aborted multipart upload or writer crash during upload. If the writer did a PutObject with zero bytes, the KMS metadata might still be present. Check CloudTrail for PutObject API around 09:15 -> was there an ETag and successful 200?
Jamal R.: also check forwarder health logs — if it attempted decrypt and hit InvalidCiphertextException, it would skip and not replay. We have a backfill/playbook to re-encrypt/replay. Steps: 
```
# replay from s3 into forwarder queue
./infra/tools/replay_audit.py --tenant 8421 --start 2026-02-12T09:12:00Z --end 2026-02-12T09:25:00Z --mode reencrypt
# or force forwarder to attempt replay on in-cluster pod
kubectl exec -n infra deploy/forwarder -- /bin/forwarder replay --tenant 8421 --manifest manifest-00023.json
```
Priya S.: I tried a head-object on a non-zero batch and got a correct size and new KMS key metadata: 
```
Key: .../shard=004/batch-000240.gz
LastModified: 2026-02-12T09:16:30Z
x-amz-meta-kms-key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222:kms/key/new-dek
ContentLength: 34129
```
So some batches were written with new-dek, others (around 09:15) are zero-byte referencing old-dek. Customer's SIEM skewer parser ignores zero-byte objects and the counts are off.
Support Oncall: quick workaround: instruct customer to include zero-byte manifests in replay (we can rehydrate via backfill). I can kick off a scoped backfill for tenant 8421 for the window.
Lucia M.: long-term fix: we need to ensure writer atomicity when KMS alias rotation occurs. Options: (a) delay rotation until writers confirm flush, (b) use envelope scheme that tolerates rotation, or (c) retry writes when PutObject returns truncated/zero size. I'll open an infra RFC.
Jamal R.: for immediate next steps: @Support Oncall please run backfill; @Priya collect a sample raw event that the customer expected (they provided event id 0e1f2a3b). We should also search whether other tenants saw similar zero-byte batches after the rotation window.
Priya S.: pasted sample raw event inline: 
```
{"id":"0e1f2a3b","type":"credential.create","tenant":8421,"ts":"2026-02-12T09:14:59Z","actor":{"id":"svc-123"},"meta":{"request_id":"req-889"}}
```
Jamal R.: noted. I'll grep forwarder metrics for `decrypt_errors` spike at 09:14-09:17 and open an incident if > threshold. Also verifying S3 lifecycle didn't prematurely delete older shards — retention_days=7 per config, so not retention.
Eng-Infra-Bot: incident created: INC-2026-1453 assigned to eng-infra, priority P2.
Priya S.: customer ok with backfill path. Can we also provide a mitigation note to avoid similar customer panic? I suggest: (1) an automated alert to ops when KMS alias rotation happens within 5 minutes of write spikes; (2) a small doc for customers about transient gaps during key rotation.
Lucia M.: agreed. I'll draft the RFC and add a small playbook snippet for urgent backfills.
Jamal R.: thanks — Support Oncall, please confirm when backfill started and paste job id. We'll follow up in this thread. :thumbsup:
Support Oncall: backfill job started (job-id bf-8421-179812) kicked at 2026-02-12T10:05Z. ETA ~20m.
Priya S.: ack, putting customer on a brief hold and will update when job completes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
